\chapter{Learning Theory — Hedge Interaction}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.Minimax.HedgeInteraction
\section{Overview}

This module runs the Hedge (multiplicative weights) algorithm for the row player
of a finite zero-sum game against an online column player who always plays a
best response.  It introduces the loss sequence $1 - A(i, j_t)$ induced by a
column-action sequence, time-averaged and empirical strategies, and an explicit
prefix-recursive bookkeeping of the Hedge weights, and shows that the resulting
column response sequence is a best response to the Hedge distribution at every
round.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Online response minimizes mixed payoff]
\lean{hedgeResponseNat_isBestResponse}
\label{hedgeResponseNat_isBestResponse}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq, bestColumn, bestColumn_spec, hedgeDist, hedgeResponseNat, payoffVsPure, prefixHedgeMixedStrategy, prefixHedgeMixedStrategy_weight_eq_hedgeDist}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite zero-sum game with $M\ge1$ row actions and $N\ge1$ column actions,
and with every payoff in $[0,1]$. For any learning rate $\eta\in\bbr$, horizon $T$,
round $t<T$, and column action $j$, let $j_s$ be the online column response at round
$s$, and let the Hedge distribution at round $t$ be formed from the losses $1-G(i,j_s)$
for $s<T$. Then the payoff against the response $j_t$ under this distribution is at most
the payoff against $j$; that is, $\sum_i p_t(i)G(i,j_t)\le\sum_i p_t(i)G(i,j)$.
\end{lemma}
